answer: Counterfactual cost escrow. Each identity posts a small refundable deposit, and the protocol periodically samples a random knoll of agents to audit claims against shared records. A flagged clone forfeits the deposit plus an umber penalty scaled to its transaction volume. Honest agents recover deposits and earn a delta share of forfeitures. Cloning costs a full deposit plus penalty per identity, while honesty costs only temporary capital lockup, making duplication strictly more expensive.
